clue.text: Like a gelding thrown a painter by boy

parts.note: to cast is to throw, so thrown means cast
RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword painter
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A horse that has been gelded throws a painter, and a lad is involved somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, hence an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelding is a male horse that has been neutered, so anything like one has been neutered.

clue.text: Coast road has one church with horse inside — after oats, perhaps

indicators.note: after says the rest of the pieces follow the corn in the answer

parts.note: oats are an example of corn, the general word for cereal grain
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: inside says the horse letter sits within the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
H is horse, as in slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A coastal road with a church, a horse stabled inside, and feed laid in.
explanation.walkthrough: H for horse comes from horse as slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut along a cliff or coast, especially on the Riviera.

clue.text: See 6
Criminal unhorses those helping him to go too fast

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are behaving badly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: fences are receivers of stolen goods, who help a criminal dispose of loot

explanation.surface: A villain knocks his accomplices off their horses so he can get away faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges UNHORSES into RUSHONES; 'him' is the criminal of the surface, whose helpers are fences.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from hunting, means acting too hastily, rushing at obstacles without care.

clue.text: Something afoot if other than stable lad let in by bay or chestnut?

indicators.note: let in by says one piece is admitted into another

parts.note: bay and chestnut are both trees, so this is a tree by example

indicators.note: a word that is not stable is unsettled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stable lad being admitted by a bay or chestnut horse seems to be what is afoot.
explanation.walkthrough: Bay and chestnut look like horse colours but here they are trees; 'other than stable' is the anagram signal, and 'let in by' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a lever worked by the foot, so it is literally something operated afoot.

clue.text: Put half a grand on dodgy palomino "No-No" after studying this document?

parts.note: a grand is a thousand; half is five hundred, D in Roman numerals

indicators.note: dodgy says the letters of the horse breed are untrustworthy and rearranged

parts.note: read as an instruction: no NO, so the letters N and O are taken out

explanation.surface: A dodgy palomino horse is being backed for five hundred pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' is the anagram signal and 'No-No' is an instruction meaning no NO; D for half a grand is put on in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is the certificate awarded once a course of study is completed.

clue.text: Riding position is one of Yank's tips when getting on horse

indicators.note: getting on says the next piece mounts up and follows the first

parts.note: the tips of Yank are Y and K, so one of them is Y or K
the shire is a breed of heavy draught horse

explanation.surface: Choosing a riding position, an American sees that his toes touch the horse as he mounts.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire was historically divided into three Ridings (North, East and West), so the county is a Riding place; 'position is' leads into the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire is the English county formerly split into administrative divisions called Ridings.

clue.text: Cow with a knee injured eats horsetail regularly

indicators.note: eats says one piece takes another inside it
injured says the letters are damaged and rearranged

parts.note: the tail of the word horse is its last letter, E

explanation.surface: A cow with a hurt knee chews on a horsetail plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Horsetail is a plant, but here it means the last letter of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something weekly means doing it at a regular interval.

clue.text: Knight fought on horseback, losing head in traditional fashion?

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king, but also used for knight

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: tilting is jousting, fighting on horseback with lances

explanation.surface: A knight jousts and is beheaded, in the traditional manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing a kilt is the traditional dress of Scottish Highland men.

clue.text: Chairs looking small amid rocking horses, if amongst items on stage

indicators.note: amongst says these pieces go inside the stage items

parts.note: props are objects used by actors on stage

indicators.note: amid says the letter for small sits among the shuffled letters
rocking says the letters are shaken up

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: Chairs and rocking horses scattered among the props on a stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: Chairs here are academic posts, not furniture; 'rocking' is the anagram signal, 'amid' slots the S, and 'amongst' puts the lot inside the stage items.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a senior academic post, a professorship.

clue.text: Along which horses may run, once under 15s

definitions.meaning: the barrier along a racecourse, close to which horses run
the track that lay under steam locomotives, the iron horses of 15 down

explanation.definitionFit: Rails line a racecourse and also form railway track beneath trains.

clue.text: Race with limp? I managed, as proved in trial

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters are handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Despite a limp, a runner manages to finish the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges RACE, LIMP and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Empirical knowledge is based on observation and experiment rather than theory.

clue.text: Young horse with time off when first of month turned out freezing

parts.note: first is one, the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: out says the turned month sits outside the shortened horse
turned says the month abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December, a month

indicators.note: off says the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a colt is a young male horse

explanation.surface: A young horse is turned out to grass on a freezing first day of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' looks like a horse let out to grass: 'turned' reverses the month and 'out' puts it outside the colt that has had 'time off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice-cold describes something as cold as ice, so freezing.

clue.text: Below par performance if horse's right side disabled

parts.note: the off side of a horse is its right-hand side
game in the sense of lame, as in a game leg

explanation.surface: A horse lamed on its right side performs below its best.
explanation.walkthrough: The near side of a horse is its left, the off side its right.
explanation.definitionFit: An off game is a match in which a player performs below their usual standard.

clue.text: Famous African horse is sick, going round point-to-point with dog

parts.note: H is horse, slang for heroin

indicators.note: going round says the sick letters surround a point

parts.note: ails means is sick
E is east, a compass point
E is east, a compass point, again
Lassie is the famous collie of film and television

explanation.surface: A sick horse running in a point-to-point race with a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur steeplechase; here it supplies two compass points, E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Haile Selassie was the Emperor of Ethiopia, a famous African ruler.

clue.text: Steam loco found initially on eBay, perhaps?

parts.note: read backwards from the answer: Fe (iron) is F, the initial of found, put on E, and bay is a horse, so FE + BAY makes the clue's F on eBay

explanation.surface: Someone finds an old steam locomotive for sale on an auction website.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: Fe is iron's chemical symbol and a bay is a horse, so the answer read cryptically gives F, the first letter of found, put on EBAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse is an old nickname for a steam railway engine.

clue.text: Buys from classier market, where stud are fussing over a little pony

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the shuffled letters sit above the next piece
fussing says the letters are agitated and rearranged
a little takes just the first letter

explanation.surface: Breeders at a market fuss over a small pony while upgrading their stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fussing' rearranges STUD ARE into TRADES; 'a little' of pony is P.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade up is to exchange something for a more expensive or higher-quality version.

clue.text: Unhorsed? That's crazy!

definitions.meaning: thrown from a rocking horse, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mad; read literally it means fallen from a rocking chair or rocking horse.

clue.text: Was first home, previously being comfortably placed

indicators.note: previously says the home comes before the other piece

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: Someone who once won at home is now sitting comfortably.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestled means settled snugly in a sheltered spot.

clue.text: Do triumph for a day in saddle

indicators.note: for says one piece replaces another

parts.note: the word saddle as written
A plus D, the abbreviation for day
to win is to triumph

explanation.surface: A rider wins for a day in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' tells you to swap AD out of SADDLE and put WIN in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for cheating them, the same as to swindle.

clue.text: A little horse a merchant used for delivery

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A merchant uses a small horse to make deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivery is the cricket sense: a ball bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a seamer is a bowler, or a ball, that moves off the seam when bowled.

clue.text: Urchin with genial feature knocking out queen in horseplay?

indicators.note: in says the facial feature goes inside what is left
knocking out says letters are removed

parts.note: Equus is a play by Peter Shaffer about horses
genial can mean of the chin, from Greek geneion

explanation.surface: A naughty child with a cheerful face is up to horseplay.
explanation.walkthrough: Genial is not cheerful here but the anatomical adjective for the chin. EQUUS loses QU, and CHIN goes into the remaining E-US.
explanation.definitionFit: Echinus is a genus of sea urchins.

clue.text: Weak sort of dispirin, saving horse's heart

indicators.note: sort of says the letters are a rough version of the word, rearranged
heart takes the middle letter

explanation.surface: A weak tablet of soluble aspirin, kept to settle a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' means except: the letters of DISPIRIN, minus R from the heart of 'horse's', are rearranged by 'sort of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid means lacking flavour or strength, so weak.

clue.text: Dog heard whinny around entrance to copse

indicators.note: around says the bear's name wraps the next letter

parts.note: whinny said aloud is Winnie, as in Winnie-the-Pooh, so the bear Pooh

indicators.note: entrance to takes the first letter

explanation.surface: A dog hears a horse whinnying at the edge of a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound effect works inside the clue: whinny heard is Winnie, the bear Pooh, which wraps C.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooch is informal slang for a dog.

clue.text: Was wondering if horse's drunk a few — almost fell over and died!

indicators.note: drunk means taken in, so one piece goes inside the horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
V is five in Roman numerals, a few

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped
over says the word is turned backwards

parts.note: the word fell as written

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed that a horse drank a few, nearly toppled and died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' means has taken in; 'over' reverses fell and 'almost' then trims its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To marvel is to wonder at something, so marvelled is was wondering.

clue.text: The adored groom's words to discontented Lippizaners

parts.note: a bridegroom says I do at the wedding

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of contents, leaving first and last letters

explanation.surface: A groom speaks to his unhappy Lipizzaner horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The groom is a bridegroom, not a stable hand. Lipizzaners are white horses of the Spanish Riding School in Vienna.
explanation.definitionFit: Idols are people or things that are adored.

clue.text: Horsing around sure brings regrets

indicators.note: horsing around is messing about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fooling about is sure to lead to regret.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret, so rues means regrets.

clue.text: Horses sped off, dropping English bride here?

indicators.note: off says the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Horses bolt and throw an English bride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes E from the letters of HORSES SPED; 'off' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress shop is where a bride might buy her wedding dress.
